questions.problem:
If
$T=[\begin{aligned}v & 2v \\ 2 & v+8\end{aligned}]$
and $det(T)=-4$, what is the value of $v?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a $2\times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}v & 2v \\ 2 & v+8\end{aligned}| \\  & =v\cdot (v+8)-2v\cdot 2 \\  & ={v}^{2}+4v\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(T)=-4$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =-4 \\ {v}^{2}+4v & =-4 \\ {v}^{2}+4v+4 & =0 \\ (v+2)^{2} & =0 \\ v & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:

$$
|\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}|=ad-bc.
$$

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(U) & =|\begin{aligned}-v & 5 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-v\cdot 3-5\cdot 4 \\  & =-3v-20\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(U)=4$, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(U) & =4 \\ -3v-20 & =4 \\ -3v & =4+20 \\ -3v & =24 \\ v & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Solving for an Unknown in an Expression Involving the Determinant of a 2x2 Matrix
canonical_examples.problem:
If
${A} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        2 & -1 \
        -3 & k
    }
    \right\rbrack$
and
$\det({A}) = 5$, what is the value of $k?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a $2 \times 2$ matrix, the determinant is given by the formula

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/ca185652796478c2c3a5bde2a7e801b7d6fd1b0ce821d571ca8b20a795147857.svg)

Using the formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -3 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot k-(-1)\cdot (-3) \\  & =2k-3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\det(A)=5,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =5 \\ 2k-3 & =5 \\ 2k & =8 \\ k & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The **determinant** of a general $2 \times 2$ matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/69a40a71c67d6e4c9bd5feff7e6dcac56fd90de45a9d97aa6562fbefc391de8e.svg)
is denoted $\text {det} ({A})$ and computed as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/f12f623d3b550dfd7819cb54e4bc76f8a711afa1fae2581ba060c57f4cd04c44.svg)

the determinant is

$$
\det(A) = {\color{blue}{2}} \cdot {\color{blue}{3}} - {\color{red}{1}} \cdot {\color{red}{5}} = 1.
$$

To remember how to compute the determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix, you can imagine taking the product of the diagonal of the matrix, and then subtracting the product of the off-diagonal terms, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/2594f99e0f02241dc6d01f85c82923103df1d6fb4dda5ca03d438637f5178a28.png)

Later, we will see that the determinant is related to the "volume" spanned by the row vectors or column vectors in a matrix. We will also see that the determinant can tell us about many other properties of a matrix. 

However, in this lesson, we will just focus on computing the determinant.

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
The **determinant** of a general $2 \times 2$ matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/69a40a71c67d6e4c9bd5feff7e6dcac56fd90de45a9d97aa6562fbefc391de8e.svg)
is denoted $\text {det} ({A})$ and computed as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/f12f623d3b550dfd7819cb54e4bc76f8a711afa1fae2581ba060c57f4cd04c44.svg)

For example, given the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/81d146203ecb2d574eb7115becb93bc190d33e0d9e093a1d7ad81c2ed7618502.svg) 
the determinant is

$$
\det(A) = {\color{blue}{2}} \cdot {\color{blue}{3}} - {\color{red}{1}} \cdot {\color{red}{5}} = 1.
$$

To remember how to compute the determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix, you can imagine taking the product of the diagonal of the matrix, and then subtracting the product of the off-diagonal terms, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14272902/assets/2594f99e0f02241dc6d01f85c82923103df1d6fb4dda5ca03d438637f5178a28.png)

Later, we will see that the determinant is related to the "volume" spanned by the row vectors or column vectors in a matrix. We will also see that the determinant can tell us about many other properties of a matrix. 

However, in this lesson, we will just focus on computing the determinant.
